newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-GRAYSON OUT, LIONS SEND FOR CATT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-GRAYSON OUT, LIONS SEND FOR CATT.

text.p: Flyhalf Paul Grayson has been ruled out of the remainder of the British Lions tour of South Africa because of injury, tour manager Fran Cotton said on Sunday.
Grayson's England colleague Mike Catt, currently with the national team in Argentina, has been called up as replacement.
"It's unfortunate and we feel very sorry for him but we just can't afford to carry anyone on the tour and we would be carrying him if he stayed," Cotton told a news conference.
Grayson suffered a thigh injury in March but was thought to have recovered sufficiently before the Lions came to South Africa.

Cotton said Grayson had aggravated the injury last Tuesday but still decided to play against Border the following day when he turned in a poor performance -- including five missed kicks at goal from five attempts in the Lions' 18-14 victory.
Catt, who scored 21 points in England's 46-20 victory over Argentina on Saturday, was a surprise omission when the Lions squad was announced.
"We faxed the England management in Buenos Aires but they obviously had a bit of a celebration last night so we haven't had a response yet," added Cotton.

"We understand the first available flight is not until Tuesday which would get him to Johannesburg on Wednesday morning. He's obviously in great form at the moment and he'll be an asset to the squad."

Catt, 25, was born in Port Elizabeth and raised in South Africa before moving to England. England loose forward Tim Rodber, a team mate of Grayson's at Northampton, said: "Paul is obviously upset, we are all sorry for him. But he is a level-headed guy, he knows he has a problem and he knows this is the best way of dealing with it."
The Lions travel to Johannesburg later on Sunday and play Mpumalanga in Witbank on Wednesday.
